steps.title: Oral rinse collection
steps.instruction: Have each donor clean the oral cavity, wait 3 min, then rinse five times with ~10 mL sterile 0.9 % NaCl for 30–60 s each, waiting 3 min between rinses to collect a total of 50 mL; immediately proceed to enrichment.

steps.title: Initial cell pelleting
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the 50 mL rinse at 160 × g, room temperature (RT), for 5–10 min. If mucus is abundant, first pass the suspension through a 40 µm sterile cell strainer.

steps.title: Supernatant removal
steps.instruction: Aspirate carefully ~40 mL supernatant without disturbing the neutrophil pellet (neutrophils do not form a solid pellet).

steps.title: Resuspend and 40 µm filter
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in the remaining ~10 mL 0.9 % saline, pass through a 40 µm sterile cell strainer by gravity to remove food particles and mucus.

steps.title: Sequential 20 µm & 10 µm filtration
steps.instruction: Filter the 40 µm‑filtered suspension sequentially through 20 µm then 10 µm pluriStrainer nylon meshes by gravity flow or 160 × g, RT, 1 min; avoid vacuum suction. After each filter, examine under an optical microscope, repeat if larger particles remain, and record cell viability and density.

steps.title: Cell counting and viability
steps.instruction: Mix 10 µL of filtered suspension with 10 µL trypan blue, load into a Countess chamber slide, and record total cells (expected ~1.8 × 10⁵ from 50 mL) and viability (70–80 %). Proceed immediately to downstream steps for unfixed cells or fix with 4 % PFA for fixed‑cell workflows.

steps.title: Prepare 384‑well lysis plates
steps.instruction: Add 2 µL lysis/FACS‑sort buffer to each well of a 384‑well thin‑walled PCR plate (exclude NTC wells); keep plates on a chill block at 4 °C.

steps.title: Set up FACS instrument
steps.instruction: Install a 100 µm (or 130 µm) nozzle, perform daily setup, test droplet delay, and plate targeting according to manufacturer instructions; ensure droplet break‑off is optimized to avoid satellite droplets.

steps.title: Confirm single‑cell targeting
steps.instruction: Run 10‑µm yellow fluorescent polystyrene microspheres (or similar beads) on the sorter, observe under a fluorescent microscope, and verify ≥95 % single‑bead sorting accuracy; perform practice sorts if needed.

steps.title: Single‑cell sorting
steps.instruction: Sort one cell into each well (except control wells) at an event rate of 1 000–2 000 events s⁻¹ for the 100 µm nozzle (≥1 200 events s⁻¹ for 130 µm). Optional: verify single‑cell deposition by microscopy of a test slide.

steps.title: Seal plates and store
steps.instruction: Seal the sorted plates with a MicroAmp Thermo‑Seal lid; either proceed immediately to lysis/RT or freeze on dry ice and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Single‑cell lysis mix addition
steps.instruction: Add to each well 0.25 µL 25 µM Oligo‑dT and 0.25 µL 25 mM dNTP mix (final 2 µL lysis buffer already present). For controls: add 1 µL 10 pg/µL UHR to UHR‑control wells, 2 µL nuclease‑free water to NTC wells, and nothing to ERCC spike‑in wells. If plates were frozen, thaw on ice in chill blocks.

steps.title: Reverse transcription master mix
steps.instruction: To the 2.5 µL lysed‑cell mixture (step 18) add 3 µL RT‑master mix (total 5.5 µL).

steps.title: RT thermocycling program
steps.instruction: Run the following program: 42 °C 90 min (RT & template‑switching), 10 cycles of 50 °C 2 min (RNA secondary‑structure unfolding), 42 °C 2 min (completion), 70 °C 15 min (enzyme inactivation), then hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: PCR pre‑amplification master mix
steps.instruction: Prepare PCR‑preamplification master mix by adding ISPCR primer as described in section 2.5.5.

steps.title: PCR pre‑amplification cycling
steps.instruction: Thermocycle: 98 °C 3 min; 21 cycles of 98 °C 20 sec, 67 °C 15 sec, 72 °C 6 min; final extension 72 °C 5 min; hold at 4 °C. Plate may be stored at –20 °C (short term) or –80 °C (long term).

steps.title: cDNA purification with AMPure XP
steps.instruction: Add AMPure XP beads (1:1 volume) to the RT reaction, incubate 5 min RT, place on magnetic rack 2 min, discard supernatant, wash beads twice with 80 % ethanol (30 sec each), air‑dry 10 sec, elute with 12.5 µL Low‑TE (10 mM Tris, 0.1 mM EDTA) for 10 min RT then 2 min on magnet. Keep beads and buffer at RT. Store purified cDNA at –80 °C or proceed to QC.

steps.title: QC1 – Agilent Bioanalyzer
steps.instruction: Load 1 µL of each randomly selected cDNA sample onto an Agilent high‑sensitivity DNA chip, run on a 2100‑Bioanalyzer, and accept libraries showing a peak at ~1.5–2 kb with no fragments <500 bp.

steps.title: QC2 – PicoGreen quantitation
steps.instruction: Prepare λ‑gDNA standards (10 ng/µL stock diluted to 10, 5, 2.5, 1.25, 0.625, 0.3125, 0.15625, 0 ng/µL). Transfer 0.50 µL purified cDNA (or standard) to each well, seal, mix, centrifuge briefly, incubate 2–5 min RT protected from light, read fluorescence on a FlexStation 3 (Ex/Em 480/520 nm), and calculate cDNA concentration from the standard curve.

steps.title: QC3 – qRT‑PCR housekeeping
steps.instruction: Dilute each cDNA 1:10 (9 µL Low‑TE + 1 µL cDNA). Prepare qRT‑PCR master mix as in section 2.5.8, dispense 7.5 µL to each well, add 2.5 µL diluted cDNA (or water for NTC). Run: 95 °C 2 min; 50 cycles of 95 °C 10 sec, 60 °C 30 sec; hold 4 °C. Analyse Ct values (threshold 0.01, baseline 2–10); Ct < 35 indicates good quality.

steps.title: QC4 – Target gene qRT‑PCR (optional)
steps.instruction: Perform TaqMan (or preferred) qRT‑PCR for a cell‑type‑specific marker on the same diluted cDNA to confirm the sorted cell identity.

steps.title: Hit‑picking of QC‑pass wells
steps.instruction: Paste cDNA concentration (from QC2) and ACTB Ct (from QC3) into the project template; select wells with cDNA > 0.3 ng/µL and Ct < 35. Generate a Hamilton input CSV, load into VENUS software, and run Hamilton transfer to a new 384‑well cDNA‑library plate. Seal, barcode, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: cDNA library normalization
steps.instruction: Thaw the hit‑picked cDNA plate on ice, transfer 1 µL from each well to a new 384‑well FrameStar plate, add Low‑TE buffer to reach 0.2 ng/µL (total volume ≤100 µL; if >100 µL, adjust to 100 µL).

steps.title: Nextera XT tagmentation
steps.instruction: Add to each well: 0.625 µL diluted cDNA (0.2 ng/µL), 1.250 µL Tagment DNA Buffer (2×), 0.625 µL Amplification Tagment Mix (ATM) – total 2.5 µL. Immediately add 0.625 µL NT buffer to neutralize (total 3.125 µL).

steps.title: Nextera PCR with indexing
steps.instruction: Add 1.875 µL NPM PCR master mix and 1.250 µL index primer mix (0.625 µL i5 + 0.625 µL i7) to the 3.125 µL tagmentation mix (final 6.25 µL). Seal, centrifuge 4 °C 500 × g (2 000 rpm) 30 sec, keep on ice. Thermocycle: 72 °C 3 min; 95 °C 30 sec; 16 cycles of 95 °C 10 sec, 55 °C 30 sec, 72 °C 60 sec; final 72 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C. Store plate at –80 °C until library cleanup.

steps.title: Nextera library purification
steps.instruction: Add AMPure XP beads at 0.9 : 1 ratio (5.625 µL beads to 6.25 µL library), incubate, magnetically separate, wash twice with 80 % ethanol, air‑dry, elute with 6.25 µL Low‑TE. Store at –80 °C.

steps.title: QC5 – Nextera PicoGreen assay
steps.instruction: Use 1 µL of each purified Nextera library in the PicoGreen assay as described in QC2 to determine library concentration.

steps.title: Normalize Nextera libraries to 1 ng/µL
steps.instruction: Dispense Low‑TE buffer to a new 384‑well plate, then add 1 µL purified Nextera library to each well using BRAVO to achieve 1 ng/µL final concentration.

steps.title: Optional 16‑sample MiSeq pooling
steps.instruction: Pool 3 µL of each of 16 normalized libraries (1 ng/µL) into a 1.5 mL LoBind tube (total 48 µL ≈ 3 ng). Add AMPure beads equal to 90 % of the pool volume, incubate, magnetically separate, wash, and elute in low‑TE at 1/10 of the original volume. Perform Agilent Bioanalyzer QC on 1:1, 1:10, and 1:20 dilutions (triplicate). Store pooled library at –20 °C.

steps.title: 384‑sample NovaSeq pooling
steps.instruction: Combine all 384 normalized libraries from a plate into a single well using BRAVO, transfer to an Eppendorf tube, and store at –20 °C (short term) or –80 °C (long term).

steps.title: Pooled library cleanup
steps.instruction: Purify the 384‑plex pool with AMPure XP beads (manual or BRAVO protocol), elute in low‑TE, and store at –20 °C (short term) or –80 °C (long term).

steps.title: QC6 – Agilent check of 384‑plex pool
steps.instruction: Load 1 µL of the pooled library onto an Agilent high‑sensitivity DNA chip, run on a 2100‑Bioanalyzer, and record fragment size and concentration; store pool at –20 °C or –80 °C until sequencing.

steps.title: QC7 – KAPA library quantification
steps.instruction: Prepare four dilution sets of the pooled library in 10 mM Tris‑HCl + 0.05 % Tween 20. Prepare qPCR master mix (1 mL Illumina Primer Premix + 5 mL KAPA SYBR Fast 2×). For half‑reaction, add 6 µL master mix + 4 µL sample or standard (4 µL water for NTC). Run on QuantStudio 6 Flex: 95 °C 5 min; 35 cycles of 95 °C 20 sec, 60 °C 45 sec; hold 4 °C. Generate a standard curve from six DNA standards (20, 2, 0.2, 0.02, 0.002, 0.0002 pM) and calculate library concentration. Verify slope (‑3.58 to ‑3.10) and R² ≈ 0.99.

steps.title: cDNA library sequencing
steps.instruction: Sequence the purified pooled Nextera library on an Illumina platform (MiSeq, HiSeq 2500, NextSeq 500, or NovaSeq 6000) using paired‑end reads (100–150 bp) to obtain ~1–2 million reads per cell.

steps.title: RNA‑seq data processing
steps.instruction: Assess raw fastq quality with FastQC; determine duplication with fastx_collapser; trim adapters and low‑quality bases with Trimmomatic; map reads to GRCh38 using HISAT2; quantify gene expression (TPM) with StringTie (gencode.v25.annotation.gtf).

steps.title: Maintain RT temperature throughout
steps.instruction: Label sterile 50 mL collection tubes, keep centrifuge set to RT, and perform all saliva neutrophil isolation steps at RT (avoid 4 °C) because neutrophils lose viability rapidly at colder temperatures.

steps.title: Final plate spin before RT
steps.instruction: Spin plates at 700 × g for 10 sec at RT, then place on ice before adding the oligo‑dT primer.

steps.title: Denature oligo‑dT annealed mix
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at 72 °C for 3 min, then immediately place on ice before proceeding to RT.
